messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to pass an array for Cafe? Actually the type says "Cafe"[] meaning an array of strings? But the enumeration includes "Cafe"[] as a type. It might mean we can pass "Cafe" as a string or an array of "Cafe"? The type is ambiguous. But likely we need to pass "Cafe" as a string. But the type says "Cafe"[] meaning an array of "Cafe". So maybe we need to pass ["Cafe"]? Let's interpret that we can pass "Cafe" as a string. But the type says "Cafe"[] meaning an array of "Cafe". So we should pass ["Cafe"].

Thus for each city:

NYC: location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

LA: location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Chicago: location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function for each city. The function returns any. We'll call it three times.
